Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Bitnomial is building the next generation US-based global derivatives exchange, starting with digital assets and progressively expanding to encompass a full spectrum of commodities worldwide. Bitnomial operates a US CFTC regulated exchange (DCM), clearinghouse (DCO), and brokerage (FCM). It offers a range of crypto-settled derivatives, including futures, options, and a suite of live perpetual futures, used by brokers, hedge funds, institutions, and trading firms around the world.

Bitnomial's exchange, clearinghouse, and brokerage systems are written largely in Haskell. In this role you will build the services and data models that record every order, fill, and settlement at a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse, with the database as a first-class part of the design. You will build features across these systems and design the schema, queries, and migrations behind them.

 

The opportunity

  • Build, test, and ship well-typed, well-reviewed features and fixes in Haskell services across the exchange, clearinghouse, and brokerage

  • Understand the order, trade, clearing, and settlement flows end to end

  • Design schema, constraints, and indexes for new features, using exact numeric types and audit trails so financial values cannot drift

  • Write migrations that are lock-safe and reversible on large tables, and review the migrations of other engineers

  • Read execution plans, find slow queries from production metrics, and fix the cause in the query, the index, or the access pattern

  • Monitor systems, respond to alerts, and support daily operations such as settlement cycles

  • Fix the cause of production issues and write down what you learned

 

What you bring

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience with a functional or strongly typed programming language such as Haskell, Rust, or C++

  • Strong SQL and PostgreSQL skills, including transactions and isolation levels

  • Solid computer science fundamentals, including data structures, concurrency, and distributed systems: replication, consistency, retries and idempotency, and how services keep shared data correct when parts fail

  • Willingness to take part in on-call and operational shifts

  • Care and rigor with code and data that move money. You measure before you tune

  • Good judgment with AI tools. You use them to work faster, and you read, test, and understand what they produce before you ship it

  • A habit of asking why before changing something

  • Sound judgment under pressure, with a calm and methodical approach when production is live

  • Collaboration across engineering, operations, risk, and compliance, with a habit of documenting

 

Nice to haves

  • Financial knowledge or experience in trading, markets, or financial services

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field, or equivalent experience

  • Haskell experience, particularly with PostgreSQL-backed services

  • Production experience with AWS Aurora PostgreSQL

  • Experience with time series or market data at volume, such as tick data, order books, or event streams

  • Experience with Atlas or another declarative schema management tool

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.

The Principal Data Operations builds and operates the systems that move Hut 8’s business and operational data from source systems into reliable, secure, analytics-ready data products.   • Strong Python and SQL skills.
  • Experience operating production data pipelines.
  • Experience with Airflow or Google Cloud Composer.
  • Experience with BigQuery, Google Cloud Storage, and Snowflake.
  • Familiarity with Git, GitHub, pull requests, automated testing, and CI/CD.
  • Linux and Bash familiarity.
  • Experience integrating REST APIs, SFTP, scheduled files, or databases.
  • Understanding of data quality, freshness, reconciliation, schema evolution, and monitoring.
  • Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

  • 3+ years of experience in data engineering, software engineering, or a related field.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

We work to deliver an excellent end-customer experience while upholding the safety and soundness of the business, so Robinhood can keep expanding access to crypto responsibly. The team partners with engineering, product, compliance, crypto operations, and enterprise risk to keep a consistent view of risk across the organization. It's an exciting time to join as we launch new products and expand our crypto offering!

As a Risk Specialist, you will support the execution of our crypto risk management program, partnering closely with Crypto Risk leadership to monitor, assess, and report on risk across the business. You will play a hands-on role in building and running operational risk management, with a particular focus on technical and product risk. Day to day, you will assess new products and business changes for risk, run risk and control self-assessments, and prepare reporting for governance forums. You will translate technical risks into clear terms for colleagues outside engineering and work closely with partner teams across the business. Your work will help us keep pace with new launches while protecting customers and the firm!

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

The Data Platform team builds and owns highly available, scalable data infrastructure for TRM's products and services. As a Senior Software Engineer on Data Infrastructure (RDBMS), you will develop, operate, and scale the relational database systems that serve data at petabyte scale, helping build a safer financial system for billions of people. This role is uniquely broad at TRM: you own the serving layer end to end, from query performance to cost to availability, on infrastructure that product teams depend on every day.

The impact you will have:

  • Keep customer-facing APIs fast and available at five-nines by owning query tuning, index design, and schema optimization on petabyte-scale Postgres/Citus, directly determining whether product teams can serve data in real time

  • Cut storage and compute costs materially by using AI-assisted analysis (pganalyze paired with Claude) to detect compression and data-model opportunities, then shipping validated changes to production

  • Remove team toil by building agentic automation for routine database operations, such as self-serve pgbouncer provisioning, disk scaling, and blue-green deployments, so any engineer can run them safely

  • Protect data integrity and latency by driving agentic validation of database changes before they reach production

  • Keep real-time data flowing by managing CDC pipelines (PeerDB, Fivetran, Debezium) and using AI tooling to debug replication failures faster

  • Shape the next-generation platform by migrating workloads off first-gen infrastructure and prototyping new data stores with AI-accelerated spikes

  • Raise the whole team's leverage by codifying your workflows into AI-native runbooks and internal tooling that teammates reuse

What we're looking for:

  • 5–8 years building and operating production PostgreSQL (Citus, Aurora, AlloyDB, or equivalent distributed Postgres)

  • Deep SQL optimization skills (Explain Plans, CTEs, window functions, partitioning, index design, query-planner behavior in distributed environments), increasingly paired with AI-assisted query analysis

  • Hands-on experience with CDC tools (PeerDB, Fivetran, Debezium, Datastream, Airbyte) and comfort using AI tooling to debug replication failure modes

  • Fluency with database profiling (pganalyze or equivalent) to interpret metrics and logs, including using LLMs to summarize performance findings

  • Production automation experience in Python or Go, including agentic automation of routine database tasks; Postgres extension development is a plus

  • Daily use of AI coding tools (Claude, Copilot) to accelerate development and produce higher-quality output faster, with the judgment to know when to trust or reject AI output

  • A track record of using AI-assisted analysis to drive measurable cost or performance improvements in production database systems

About the Team:

  • The Data Platform team is distributed, not distant. We operate async-first across US and Canada working hours with intentional synchronous touchpoints when speed demands it

  • We own the petabyte-scale data infrastructure that powers TRM's products. The scope is large, the mission is real, and the work is technically demanding

  • Team culture is product-focused, customer-focused, coaching-oriented, scrappy when needed, and process-oriented when executing against OKRs

  • You will work alongside senior engineers who care deeply about their craft and hold high standards for code quality, operational excellence, and cross-team communication

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • Distributed, not distant: most collaboration happens async in Slack, Notion, and GitHub, and meetings are purposeful and minimal

  • Primary timezone overlap across US and Canada working hours; our north star is no IC spending more than 3–4 hours per week in meetings

  • Written-first culture: technical specs and decision docs drive alignment before code

On Call Requirements:

  • ⚠️ On Call Requirements — Pending Regional Compliance Review. This role carries an on-call rotation (approximately once every 15 days; each shift is a 24-hour window across 2 days). On-call is clear to proceed for United States; the Canada portion requires People Ops / Deel provincial confirmation before this section is finalized and posted. See the On-Call Compliance note in the Post-Fill Summary.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within 30 days, eliminate a single point of failure by shipping self-serve scaling automation (pgbouncer provisioning, disk resizing) that any teammate can run, freeing senior engineering time

  • Within the first quarter, identify a compression opportunity with AI-assisted analysis, validate it with a proof of concept, and ship it to production for a measurable storage-cost reduction with zero availability impact

  • Within 90 days, coordinate a schema change across three product-engineering teams in parallel and deliver the platform changes ahead of a product deadline so a customer feature ships on time

Work Week Travel: This role requires participation in in-person R&D work weeks, typically 1–2 times per quarter, at a TRM hub or other designated location. Work weeks may be scheduled with as little as 14 days’ notice, and some roles may require additional travel based on team and cross-functional needs. TRM coordinates and covers approved travel, lodging, and workspace. Accommodations are available for legitimate caregiving, health, immigration, and similar constraints.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy and Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.
descriptions.job-055fe9p:
About Mesh

At Mesh, our mission is to enable consumers to pay and be paid with any asset. Today, trillions of dollars in tokenized assets exist but remain largely unusable for everyday commerce. Mesh is bridging this gap by making crypto payments reliable, useful, and ubiquitous. We combine a powerful orchestration engine with a seamless consumer app to unlock liquidity for the world. Backed by leading investors like SBI, Money Forward, Paradigm, Dragonfly, Galaxy, and PayPal Ventures, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of the global economy. Join us!

Overview

You will own Mesh's numbers and its operating agenda. You run the budget, forecast and board financials, lead the financial side of acquisitions and capital decisions, and drive the company's operating cadence: OKRs, a business review every two weeks, and clear, data-backed calls on what is working and what isn't. You lead the team that builds our revenue and finance systems.

We want someone who is all about the numbers and works directly in the data, brings structure, holds leaders to their commitments, and is comfortable challenging senior people directly.

What You'll Do

  • Own the annual budget and monthly forecast across ten departments; rollout quarterly budget review calls. 
  • Build and maintain a driver-based operating model: payment volume, take rates, contract minimums, subsidies, headcount and vendor spend.
  • Own the quarterly board financials and monthly management pack: revenue, gross margin, spend vs. budget, burn, runway and cash.
  • Own the monthly P&L flux review and commentary and assembly of the financial statement package with the accounting team.
  • Run the business review in coordination with BizOps, monthly and the quarterly OKR reviews, track commitments and call out misses with data.
  • Own the company's metric definitions and the payments metrics we manage to, so every leader presents from the same numbers.
  • Do the hands-on analysis behind those metrics. Pull, model and interpret the data yourself using Claude and other AI tools, with the platform data team providing access and support.
  • Run the financial workstream on acquisitions with Corporate Development: models, valuation, synergy and integration cases, DD, and coordination.
  • Lead capital allocation analysis: returns on new products, corridors and incentives such as rate subsidies, and build vs. buy.
  • Plan capital for licensed entities: project net worth and EU capital headroom and flag funding needs early.
  • Approve pricing exceptions outside the agreed deal guardrails.
  • Build the sales capacity and quota model with the CRO as part of the budget.  
  • Support org design and cross-functional programs for the CFO.
  • Lead the Manager of FinOps, RevOps & Finance Systems.
  • Confirm budget availability on purchase orders above the approval threshold.

Metrics You'll Own

  • Volume: total payment volume by product, active transacting accounts, volume per account, customer concentration.
  • Monetization: net revenue, take rate (actual vs. contracted), usage against minimum commitments, revenue per account.
  • Unit economics: cost per transaction, subsidies and incentives in basis points, net take rate, contribution margin per customer.
  • Retention: gross and net revenue and volume retention by cohort, logo churn, silent churn (live accounts down more than 50% from peak).
  • Growth: new logos, time from signing to go-live and to first transaction, ramp to committed volume, pipeline coverage, win rate, committed ARR vs. run-rate revenue.
  • Efficiency and cash: CAC payback, burn multiple, DSO, bad debt.

Who You Are

  • 8+ years combining strategy consulting (Big Four strategy practice or similar), investment banking, private equity or FP&A, with at least 2–4 years operating in-house at a fintech or payments company.
  • A budget process you ran end to end with department leaders, and board-level reporting you owned.
  • Strong modeling, including M&A or investment models.
  • An operating cadence or OKR process you built and ran across functions.
  • Hands-on with data and AI: uses Claude and similar tools to pull, model and analyze data and build reporting directly, since there is no analytics team to hand it to.
  • The presence to challenge senior leaders with data and keep the relationship

Nice to have

  • Crypto experience.
  • Capital planning for regulated entities.
  • Experience managing systems or data builders.

What success looks like

  • 90 days: own the FY27 budget and run its first reforecast; metric dictionary agreed by the CFO, CRO and Product; business review running every two weeks on one set of numbers; next board financials delivered on time and tied to the books.
  • 6 months: quarterly budget reviews with every department; OKRs set and reviewed quarterly; unit economics by product; diligence model template used on every deal.

The compensation range provided may span multiple career levels and will be narrowed during the interview process based on factors including a candidate's experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location. For candidates outside of New York or San Francisco, compensation will be adjusted to reflect the applicable market and location-based pay band. The base salary range listed excludes commission (if applicable), equity, and benefits. The pay range represents the minimum and maximum target for new-hire compensation. Actual compensation may vary and may be higher or lower depending on individual circumstances.

Pay Range
$220,000—$250,000 USD

Why You’ll Love It Here

At Mesh, you're not stepping into a typical role—you're joining a rocket ship in mid-liftoff. You'll tackle complex, meaningful problems that actually move an industry forward, working alongside a sharp, motivated team that moves quickly, collaborates deeply, and expects everyone to operate with ownership. This is the kind of place where you'll see your work ship fast, make real impact, and be able to point to something and say, "I built that." You'll grow fast, level up your skills, and get a front-row seat to how a high-growth company scales from the inside, with competitive comp, solid benefits, and room to stretch your craft all coming standard. If you're energized by building, learning, and shaping something big—this is where you'll want to be.

In-Office Expectations

Employees based in our San Francisco, New York, and Bangalore hubs are expected to work from the office at least 40% of the time (approximately two days per week). This expectation may vary slightly depending on role, team, and business needs. Certain roles that require closer cross-functional collaboration or operational support may have additional in-office requirements, which will be discussed during the interview process. Our hybrid approach is designed to balance meaningful in-person collaboration, team building, and real-time decision-making with the flexibility to work remotely. We believe this structure supports strong execution while preserving autonomy and focus time.

How We Care For Our Team

We believe great work happens when people feel valued and supported. That starts with competitive salary and equity that grows as you and the company grow, plus comprehensive health coverage for you and your family. We offer unlimited PTO—and we mean it. Take the time you need to recharge and show up at your best.

We're invested in your growth with a dedicated budget for courses, conferences, and certifications. Work from wherever you're most productive with our remote-friendly approach, and count on having the top-tier tools and equipment you need to do exceptional work.

Mesh Pay is committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, genetic information, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, lawful alien status, national origin, age, marital status, and non-job related physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Role

As a Senior DevOps Engineer you will design, build and operate the platforms behind software delivery, edge and L7 networking, platform access, and the application-facing parts of our observability stack. Alpaca is expanding fast and our needs grow with it, so we run a follow-the-sun model that keeps those systems covered around the clock. This role is the team's presence in its own region: supporting and owning that platform in your timezone.

While we are not looking for a specialist in a single tool, deep expertise in one of the tools we use alongside a broad skillset would be an advantage. What we care about most is judgement: thinking in terms of delivery and the request path, understanding business priorities and the pressure that comes with fast growth, and carrying a piece of work across quarters to a high standard without needing supervision. The engineers who do well here choose the simple solution over the easy one, even when the simple one takes longer to find.

Things You Get To Do

  • Help the engineers who build on our platform: troubleshoot problems across the stack, advise teams on how to use what we run, and take your share of the support rotation during your region's hours.
  • Participate in our Follow-The-Sun on-call model: watch and triage alerts, join and declare incidents, lead structured debugging and escalation, and drive blameless post-mortems and the post-actions that actually close the loop.
  • Own the path a change takes to production - GitHub Actions into Argo CD, with Helm underneath - and the release tooling that has to work across multiple clusters and regions.
  • Run high-traffic edge and API gateway infrastructure serving hundreds of millions of requests a day globally, where performance, availability and safe change all matter at once.
  • Operates the internal tooling the rest of engineering depends on - Grafana, Sentry, Teleport, Metabase, Atlantis and others - as production services with real users rather than one-off installations.
  • Advance Platform-as-a-Product: build self-serve capabilities and paved paths so engineers can get what they need through a golden path rather than a hand-off, measured by how quickly and safely the rest of engineering can ship.
  • Take improvement projects end to end, from a problem nobody has framed yet through to something running in production that other teams rely on.

Who You Are (Must-Haves)

  • 5+ years in a DevOps, Platform/Infrastructure, or SRE role, with a proven track record operating large-scale, high-availability, high-performance systems in production.
  • A track record of carrying multi-quarter platform work end to end in a complex environment running multiple Kubernetes clusters.
  • Deep production Kubernetes experience across multiple clusters - upgrades, debugging and day-to-day operational ownership - including packaging and deploying workloads with Helm.
  • Strong Infrastructure-as-Code skills with Terraform, structuring codebases across multiple environments, with GitOps as a first principle and least-privilege as a default mindset.
  • Proven experience building and owning CI/CD pipelines at scale, for example with GitHub Actions, including releases that deploy to multiple production locations rather than only promoting through environments.
  • GitOps continuous delivery with Argo CD, or a comparable tool you can transfer from.
  • Working production experience on Google Cloud, ideally GKE. You do not need to have designed landing zones or cloud topology, but you should be fluent operating on GCP day to day.
  • Solid L7 networking fundamentals - load balancing, DNS, TLS and HTTP routing - and comfort debugging the request path from edge to workload.
  • A Platform-as-a-Product mindset, treating what the team runs as products with real users rather than internal installations.
  • Able and willing to take part in a Follow-The-Sun on-call rotation from APAC or EMEA hours, and to work effectively in a distributed, async-first team with strong written communication.

Who You Might Be (Bonus Points)

You can succeed in this role without all of the below, but any of these will help you ramp faster:

  • Policy-as-code and IaC quality tooling (OPA/Conftest, Checkov, tflint, Atlantis, or similar).
  • Experience managing Terraform state, module registries and versioning at scale across many teams.
  • Running secret management at scale (HashiCorp Vault, OpenBao, or similar) as a service other teams depend on.
  • Internal PKI and certificate lifecycle management (private CAs, issuance and rotation, mTLS between services).
  • Experience building self-serve developer platforms and internal golden paths (e.g. with Backstage, Tilt, or similar).
  • Production experience on Azure alongside GCP.
  • Working proficiency in Go for automation and tooling.
  • Strong Linux (Debian/Ubuntu) and container (Docker/containerd) fundamentals.
  • Security and compliance experience in a regulated environment (SOC 2, audit logging).
  • Familiarity with trading, brokerage, or other regulated fintech domains.

How We Take Care of You:

  • Competitive Salary & Stock Options
  • Health Benefits
  • New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500
  • Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card

Alpaca is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to pursuing and hiring a diverse workforce.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

We're creating an entirely new payments platform, built with stablecoins, to simplify global money movement. Bridge enables faster, cheaper payments and borderless access to dollars via stablecoins. Through our APIs, businesses can send and receive funds across borders faster and cheaper vs. SWIFT and other fiat-only rails. Our virtual accounts enable international consumers and businesses to easily access, store, and spend US dollars. Our payouts infrastructure enables platforms to disburse USD to anyone globally. We believe many trillions of dollars will move and settle through stablecoin payment rails. Bridge is pulling this future forward.

We have a small team of people who have previously built financial infrastructure at some of the world's leading companies (Coinbase, Stripe, Square, Brex, Upstart, DoorDash, Airbnb), and each and every one of them chose Bridge because they fundamentally believe that stablecoins will be a critical piece of financial infrastructure that allows for the improvement of global money movement.

What you'll do

We're hiring a Security Engineer to build and scale the Bridge security foundation. This is a rare opportunity to design a security program from the ground up, while also leveraging the infrastructure, best practices, and tooling of one of the most mature security organizations in the industry.

Responsibilities

  • Design and implement the Bridge security roadmap from first principles to production.
  • Identify and tackle the most important Bridge security risks quickly and pragmatically.
  • Integrate with Stripe infrastructure where it makes sense, and find custom solutions where it doesn't.
  • Lead threat modeling and hardening efforts for the Bridge money movement systems in collaboration with crypto and infra teams.
  • Build key security capabilities, including monitoring, secrets management, incident response, access controls, and CI/CD hardening.
  • Reinforce engineering best practices around secure development and infrastructure.
  • Ensure Bridge meets compliance and audit expectations as we scale to more regulated markets.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering, product, and the Stripe security organization to move fast without compromising safety.

Who you are

Minimum requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in Security engineering.
  • Experience building or scaling security programs at a startup or in an embedded role.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in fast-paced startup environments, building security practices from the ground up.
  • Startup mindset—scrappy, pragmatic, and quick to solve the most critical problems.
  • Comfort writing and debugging backend application code, with Ruby experience preferred.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and ability to ruthlessly prioritize.
  • Ability to balance security rigor with speed, especially in fast-moving environments.
  • Clear communication across technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Interest in the potential of crypto and stablecoins to power global financial infrastructure.
descriptions.job-068ybst:
Own Your Intelligence

 

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

 

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

 

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators — including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.

Role Impact

Computer-use agents must understand changing interfaces, maintain intent over long workflows, recover from mistakes, manage permissions and side effects, and know when an outcome is actually complete. You will build post-training and evaluation systems for multimodal agents operating browsers, desktops, and cross-application workflows. The work is grounded in an active external program. The research challenge is turning real workflows and traces into environments, rewards, and experiments that produce reliable improvement.

Responsibilities

Applied Research at Prime

We turn a workflow into tasks, environments, evaluations, and reward signals, run post-training experiments against real baselines, and deploy what works. When a result looks good, we find out whether the gain came from the model or from the data, harness, inference, or infrastructure. The reusable parts become shared research, open-source systems, and product capabilities.

Every Applied Research role is externally facing. Most researchers work directly with customers, users, or research partners while maintaining a substantive research agenda.

Representative early problems

  • Build long-horizon computer-use environments from real workflows while preventing shortcuts, leakage, and unsafe side effects.

  • Train agents to recover from interface changes, partial failures, and ambiguous intermediate states instead of restarting or silently drifting.

  • Develop evaluations that distinguish genuine completion from plausible-looking behavior, including correctness, efficiency, permissions, and appropriate escalation.

What you will own

  • Multimodal environments built from partner workflows, demonstrations, tools, interface state, and outcome criteria.

  • Browser, desktop, and cross-application agents with reliable sandbox and boundary enforcement.

  • Training and evaluation from demonstrations, interventions, production failures, synthetic tasks, and verifiable outcomes.

  • Experiments on recovery and generalization across applications, layouts, permissions, and deployment contexts.

Requirements

  • Relevant experience: multimodal agents, computer use, browser or desktop automation, RL, imitation learning, HCI, embodied agents, or long-horizon agent evaluation.

  • Hands-on experience building and debugging model-training, post-training, agent, evaluation, or closely adjacent experimental loops.

  • Strong experimental judgment: meaningful baselines, careful trace inspection, clear failure attribution, and a willingness to change direction when the evidence changes.

  • Strong Python and the ability to build artifacts that other researchers and engineers can run, inspect, and extend.

  • Comfort owning ambiguous problems and keeping partners and teammates current as you resolve them.

Evidence of exceptional work

We value publications, open-source systems, benchmarks, and shipped products as evidence of exceptional work. Show us something difficult you built, what failed, and how the evidence changed your approach.

Benefits and Perks

  • Cash Compensation Range of $150-300k + equity incentives

  • Flexible Work (San Francisco, New York, London, or remote)

About HIFI

HIFI is a stablecoin infrastructure company building technology for the next-generation of financial products. We build tools for payments and tokenized money products across money movement, cards, and capital markets. Institutions and enterprises already use our platform and APIs to move billions of dollars in production environments around the world, and we are still early.

 

Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

 

About the Team

HIFI's engineering team builds the payments infrastructure that fintechs and financial institutions use to move money on stablecoin rails. The team owns the APIs, ledger, and on-chain systems behind every payment HIFI processes, and works closely with product and compliance to make sure that infrastructure is reliable, secure, and ready for regulated use. As HIFI's volume grows and more institutions build on our platform, this team will decide how stablecoin payments hold up at the scale and standard that traditional financial infrastructure is held to.

 

As a Blockchain Engineer at HIFI you will help own on-chain systems day to day. You'll build and maintain the integrations, smart contracts, and wallet infrastructure that connect HIFI's payments products to the chains and stablecoins we support. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you'll design how funds move and settle on-chain, work with the rest of engineering to connect those flows to our ledger and APIs, and partner with compliance on controls like wallet screening and transaction monitoring. You'll also be the person the team relies on to judge when a new chain or protocol is ready for production use.

 

What you will build

  • Wallet infrastructure, including key management, transaction signing, and orchestration across custodial and programmatic wallets.

  • Onchain transaction handling across EVM chains and the other networks we support, including gas, nonce management, and retries.

  • Stablecoin minting, burning, and settlement logic that connects USDC and other stablecoins to fiat rails for our on-ramp and off-ramp products.

  • Integrations with centralized and decentralized exchanges for swaps and liquidity routing, and cross-chain bridging between networks.

  • A double-entry ledger that keeps onchain balances, banking partners, and customer accounts in sync, with automated reconciliation.

  • Event listeners, confirmation tracking, and webhooks that give our platform and customers real-time visibility into onchain activity.

  • Idempotent transaction pipelines with failure recovery and screening hooks, so money moves correctly even when something goes wrong.

 

You might be a fit if

  • 3+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 1 to 2 years building blockchain systems in production.

  • Deep familiarity with EVM chains, including transaction lifecycles, gas mechanics, common failure modes, and enough Solidity to read and integrate contracts.

  • Experience with wallet architecture, such as custody models, signing services, or MPC and HSM-backed setups.

  • Strong backend fundamentals, including API design, data modeling, and handling consistency and concurrency in distributed systems.

  • You build financial systems with reconciliation and audit trails by default.

  • You communicate clearly in code review and in writing.

 

Nice to have

  • Experience with stablecoin infrastructure such as Circle, or with connecting onchain and fiat settlement.

  • Hands-on work with CEX APIs, DEX protocols like Uniswap, or bridge integrations.

  • Experience building ledgers or double-entry accounting systems.

  • Exposure to compliance engineering, such as transaction monitoring, address screening, or Travel Rule tooling.

  • Experience with non-EVM chains like Solana or Tron.

  • Familiarity with traditional money movement, including ACH, wires, and how funds settle between banks and processors.

  • Early-stage startup experience building and running a system from scratch.

 

Why This Role Matters

Every payment HIFI processes eventually settles on-chain, and the institutions behind those payments expect them to work as reliably as a wire or an ACH transfer. This is a chance to build the on-chain systems that hold stablecoin payments to that standard, and to shape how regulated money moves on public blockchains while that infrastructure is still being defined.

Must be within a commutable distance from our office and able to work in person most days of the week.
